top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

    concurrency:

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

    concurrency:

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

The VSS Blueprint uses vision language models (VLMs) such as NVIDIA Cosmos, LLMs such as NVIDIA Nemotron, RAG, and NVIDIA NIMs.

top_findings.message: 2 findings — e.g. Possible slack_token found.; Possible aws_access_key_id found.
top_findings.fix_hint:
ROTATE the leaked credential immediately (don't just delete it
from the file — assume it's compromised the moment it touched
git). Then remove it from history (`git filter-repo`) and
configure a secrets scanner (`gitleaks`, GitHub secret scanning)
to prevent recurrence.

top_findings.message: 5 findings — e.g. Hotspot: deploy/helm/developer-profiles/dev-profile-search/values.yaml changed 108 times and is >500 lines.; Hotspot: .github/workflows/ci.yml changed 108 times and is >500 lines.
top_findings.fix_hint:
For each hotspot, identify the dominant axes of change (e.g. one
file holds both API routing and validation logic) and split along
those lines. After the split, both halves see lower per-file churn.

top_findings.message: README has no fenced code blocks (agents cannot copy commands verbatim).
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add three short sections to README: Install (one fenced block),
Run (one fenced block showing the canonical entry point), Test
(one fenced block). Three fenced blocks is the floor; if your
project genuinely needs more, write more.

top_findings.message: No project manifest found (pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, ...).
top_findings.fix_hint:
Drop a `pyproject.toml` (or `package.json` / `Cargo.toml` / etc.)
at the repo root with at least name + version + dependencies. For
monorepos, every package directory should have its own manifest.

top_findings.message:
A workflow does `git push` and no workflow has a top-level
`concurrency:` block. The self-pushing workflow can race itself.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Add a `concurrency:` block at the top of any workflow that does
`git push`. Use a stable group name (e.g. the workflow file name) so
multiple runs of the same workflow serialise. For write workflows,
set `cancel-in-progress: false`:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}
      cancel-in-progress: false

Combine with `git pull --rebase` before the `git push` so the second
run picks up the first run's commit instead of failing on a non-fast
forward.

top_findings.message: .gitignore covers 4/7 groups; missing: dist_build, python_egg_info, coverage.
top_findings.fix_hint:
Generate a `.gitignore` for your stack (e.g. https://gitignore.io)
and paste the result. At minimum, every repo needs the universal
groups (`.env`, IDE state, `*.log`); the rest are scored against
the detected primary language only.
